Montréal Communiqué 


June 15, 1970 
For release at will 


Approximately 170 words 


YMCA DUAL THRUST 
IMPOSES NEW STRAINS 


Efforts to cope with a mounting workload helped sharpen 
and temper the capabilities of the Montreal YMCA during the 
year ended May 31, 1970 

"Resources were concentrated with telling impact in two 
major areas: building-based programs and outreach activities,” 
state W.S. Kirkpatrick, president, and R.G. Rogers, general 
secretary, in the Association's latest annual report. 

Major operations of the Montreal YMCA are carried on 
by four full-facility branches, four community branches, a 
camping branch (three camping facilities), a 500-room 
residence and a metropolitan outreach unit. 

During the year, city-wide activities involved some 
55,000 persons of all ages. 

Branch-based programs filled a wide range of needs. 
Some of them provided youth and adults with satisfying 
outlets for leisure time energies. Others encouraged 
self-development. Perhaps best-known of all were fitness- 
promoting activities. 


«- more 


~2= 


Under the heading of ‘outreach', the Y initiated and 
integrated a number of undertakings affecting 4 diversified 
range of community concerns, particularly as they pertain to 
youth. 

"Many of the problems would have been self-perpetuating 
if ignored, compounding the costs of dealing with them in 
the future,” say Messrs. Kirkpatrick and Rogers.
